diagnosis: Attrition bias from differential loss to follow-up
mechanism: Attrition bias is a selection bias that arises when losses to follow-up differ systematically between comparison groups or are related to prognosis/outcome, so the participants remaining for analysis are no longer comparable to those originally enrolled.
vignette: A randomized trial compares two long-term treatments for chronic pain. Participants assigned to one treatment who experience poor symptom control are much more likely to stop attending follow-up visits than participants in the other group. The final analysis includes only participants with complete follow-up data.
lead: Which of the following biases most directly threatens the validity of the treatment comparison?
distractor_notes: Recall bias arises from differential accuracy of remembered prior exposures and is not caused by systematic dropout during follow-up.
Lead-time bias concerns apparent survival prolongation from earlier diagnosis without changing time of death.
Verification bias occurs when application of a diagnostic reference standard depends on an index-test result or clinical suspicion.
Immortal time bias occurs when a period during which an outcome cannot occur is incorrectly assigned to an exposure group.
key_expl: Differential loss to follow-up can destroy the comparability created at randomization, especially when dropout is related to treatment response or prognosis. Restricting the analysis to participants who remain under observation can therefore produce a biased treatment effect. This is attrition bias, a form of selection bias.
objective: Recognize attrition bias when differential, outcome-related loss to follow-up changes the composition of comparison groups.
